title: Fourier concentration on a small family
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. For real numbers $\epsilon,\eta>0$ and an integer $k\ge0$, suppose its total influence $I(f)$ is positive and the sum of squared Fourier coefficients over sets of size greater than $k$ is at most $\epsilon$. Set $\rho=\eta/(2+\eta)$ and $\tau=((\epsilon/I(f))\rho^k)^{1+\eta}$, and let $J$ be the coordinates whose pivotal probabilities are at least $\tau$. The sum of squared Fourier coefficients over all sets that are not both contained in $J$ and of size at most $k$ is at most $2\epsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube to the signs
The total influence of $f$ is positive
The Fourier weight on sets of size greater than $k$ is at most $\epsilon$
